senses.gloss: ādya-stamba, ‘covered with original shrubs’, i. e. yielding no revenue income, never cultivated.
ā-mā, abbreviation of ādya-māṣa (i.e. the original māṣa of 5 ratis).
Balisādhaka, tax-collector (Ghoshal, Ag. Syst., p. 25).
Bṛhad-aśvavāra, a cavalry officer (Tripathi, History of Kanauj, p. 137).
daivaka see rājaka-daivaka.
deva-hala, same as deva-bhoga-hala; cf. hala-nyāya, bhikṣu-hala. See Suc. Sāt., pp. 84, etc.
Digvijayin, ‘the conqueror of the quarters’; title of some rulers conventionally claiming to have conquered the cakravarti- kṣetra (q. v.).
dukra, (1/5) of a phadiyā.
hala-nyāya, custom followed in granting rent-free holdings; same as brahmadeya-maryādā, etc.
kedāra, coin of the Kidāra-Kuṣāṇas (Bhandarkar, Carm. Lect., 1921, p. 205).
laṅkā, islet in a river (Kākatīyasaṃcika, No. 31).
Nigrāhaka, tax-collector (Ghoshal, Ag. Syst., p. 25). cf. Koṭṭa-nigraha.
nivāta see s-oṣar-āvaskara-sthāna-nivāta-lavaṇ-ākara (EI 22); same as āvāta.
pañcāṅgula, impression the plam with outstretched fingers dipped in sandal paste or any such thing; also called Pañcāṅgulika.
Pāṭīpati (Tripathi, History of Kanauj, p. 137); cf. Pāṭyuparika.
prasūti-śālā, maternity home (Kākatīyasaṃcika, No. 31).
putra, cf. Kerala-putra, king of the Keralas; Guhila-putra, descendant of Guhila.
siṃhakara, ‘lion-tax’ (Ghoshal, HRS, p. 232).
utpratikara, same as apratikara (Ep. Ind., Vol. XIX, p. 54, line 10).
utthāpita, dedicated (E. I., 16, p. 15).
vṛndāvana, see bṛndāvana.
Vyantara, see Yakṣa.
Yāma-ceṭī (Tripathi, History of Kanauj, p. 137), probably, a female attendant to the ghaṭī-yantra (q. v.); cf. Yāmakinī.
Yāmakinī, cf. Yāma-ceṭī.
s̤as̤ghānī , Tughlaq coin, 4 jītals in weight and value.
ṣaḍ-voḍḍika-dramma (JUPHS, Vol. XVIII, p. 200), copper dramma equal to 6 voḍḍikas or 120 cowrie-shells.
